images.title: Rule digits out first
images.purpose: Show the first move in the lock puzzle: the clue with nothing correct removes three digits at once.
images.composition: A padlock with three empty code windows on the left, a row of ten digit tiles on the right with three struck out, and one caption line; wide margins.
exact_structure: Left: one flat padlock outline in grey (#6B7280) with exactly 3 empty windows, each showing a teal (#0072B2) question mark.
Right: exactly 10 square digit tiles in one row, 0 to 9 in order.
Tiles 0, 3 and 6 are filled light grey (#6B7280) with a grey diagonal strike; the other 7 tiles are white with teal (#0072B2) outlines.
Above the tiles, one caption line in reddish purple (#CC79A7): 0 3 6: nothing is correct.
The code itself is not shown anywhere.
rejection: any digit shown in the padlock windows
struck tiles other than exactly 0, 3 and 6
images.takeaway: Start with the clue that rules digits out, then work with the digits that remain.
images.description: A padlock with three question marks beside digit tiles 0 to 9, with 0, 3 and 6 struck out.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which clue to use next once 0, 3 and 6 are gone.

image_decisions.why: A visual of ruling digits out helps students start the puzzle without giving the code.
